- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially in early horizon.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes (e.g., 75+), especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative — cap forecast at 1–2% below peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct — adjust forecast to align with recent 5-day average.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overreacting to short-term sentiment shifts — dampen early forecast peaks if sentiment turns negative within 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– cycles, model tends to lag — adjust forecast to match sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead, not 3–5.
